research.title: TrustClinAI: Evaluating the Trustworthiness of Clinical AI
research.description: Designed a multidimensional auditing protocol evaluating clinical risk predictors across predictive performance, calibration, explainability, and data robustness axes.
notes: Audited predictors across performance, calibration, explainability and robustness rather than accuracy alone.
SHAP attribution isolated clinically costly false negatives — the failure mode a single accuracy metric hides.

research.title: GraphBRAIN-ABIDE
research.description: Benchmark comparing 3 classical ML models against 5 GNN architectures modeling functional brain connectomes from rs-fMRI data across 848 subjects and 19 sites.
notes: 5 GNN architectures: GCN-ResNet, GATv2, ChebNet, BrainGNN, Population GCN
Analysis of domain shift and out-of-distribution generalization

caseStudy.brief: Does a graph neural network actually generalise better than classical ML on functional connectomes, or does site-level domain shift do the work? 848 subjects across 19 ABIDE I sites, one like-for-like benchmark.
approach: Built functional connectome graphs from rs-fMRI time series for every subject in ABIDE I.
Trained five GNN architectures — GCN-ResNet, GATv2, ChebNet, BrainGNN and Population GCN — against three classical baselines.
Evaluated with 19-fold leave-one-site-out cross-validation so no site appeared in both training and test data.
Measured the drop under domain shift and on held-out sites instead of reporting pooled accuracy.
results: A like-for-like comparison across 848 subjects and 19 sites, with every architecture trained and scored under the same protocol.
Leave-one-site-out numbers show how much pooled accuracy came from site-level regularities rather than disease signal.
Code and evaluation setup released on GitHub for reproduction.

projects.title: Livora AI
projects.subtitle: Liver Health Screening Platform
projects.metric: 97% ultrasound accuracy · OCR reports · deterministic lab scoring
projects.description: Multimodal diagnostic platform integrating MobileNetV2 CNN with 97% accuracy, OCR-based lab report extraction, deterministic clinical calculators, and a safety-gated AI assistant.
highlights: 97% accuracy classifying liver ultrasound scans (HCC, Hemangioma)
Deterministic FIB-4 and APRI clinical calculators to prevent LLM hallucinations
Safety-gated generative AI with red-flag triage engine for clinical emergencies

caseStudy.brief: A liver screening tool has to be useful in a clinic, not only accurate on a test set: take an ultrasound and a lab report, and return a risk assessment a patient can act on — without letting a language model invent a clinical number.
approach: Trained a MobileNetV2 classifier on liver ultrasound scans to separate HCC from hemangioma, reaching 97% accuracy.
Extracted lab values from uploaded reports with OCR, then computed FIB-4 and APRI in deterministic code instead of asking a model to produce them.
Gated the generative assistant behind a red-flag triage engine, so an emergency surfaces as an explicit warning rather than conversational text.
Shipped the pipeline as a Flask service backed by PostgreSQL, with the model, calculators and assistant sharing one request path.
results: 97% classification accuracy on the ultrasound test split.
Clinical indices are reproducible because they are computed in code, not generated as prose.
When a lab value is missing, the report shows a gap instead of a confident hallucination.

projects.title: IBM Bob 2.0
projects.subtitle: Autonomous Legacy & Security Modernizer
projects.description: Multi-agent platform that points at a polyglot repository, finds vulnerabilities through AST taint-flow analysis, cross-references CVE advisories via RAG, writes patches, gates them behind a structural safety check and a three-agent approval debate, then executes them in an isolated Docker sandbox with automatic repair.
highlights: Auditor benchmark: precision 0.909, recall 1.000 with zero false negatives, F1 0.952
AST safety gate blocks eval/exec/os.system and Big-O regressions before a patch can merge
Sandbox test failures trigger automatic repair from parsed tracebacks, up to five attempts

caseStudy.brief: A polyglot legacy repository with known vulnerabilities: find them across languages, patch them, and prove the patch does not break the build — with no human in the loop until the change is verified.
approach: Wrote an AST taint-flow auditor that traces untrusted input to dangerous sinks across languages.
Cross-referenced findings against CVE advisories through a FAISS retrieval layer.
Gated every generated patch behind a structural safety check that blocks eval, exec, os.system and Big-O regressions before the patch can merge.
Ran a three-agent approval debate, executed the patch in an isolated Docker sandbox, and repaired from parsed tracebacks up to five attempts.
results: Auditor benchmark: precision 0.909, recall 1.000, F1 0.952 — zero false negatives on the benchmark set.
28 of 28 sandbox tests passed on the released patch set.
Every change keeps an audit trail: finding, CVE reference, patch, safety verdict and test run.
